key_insight: A fully mixed finite element formulation can stably and accurately couple viscoelastic Kelvin--Voigt mechanics with reaction-diffusion calcium signaling through two-way mechanochemical feedback.
engineering_relevance: This gives solid-mechanics and bioengineering simulations a provably well-posed tool for predicting how tissue deformation and calcium waves influence each other in 2D and 3D.
method: Model mechanics with elastic/viscous stresses, velocity, and spin as mixed unknowns; enforce weak stress symmetry.
Model calcium and inactivated IP3 transport in mixed form by adding the diffusive flux as an unknown.
Use a general semidiscrete FEM framework with one inf-sup condition and a commuting interpolation operator to obtain optimal error estimates.
evidence_signal: The paper reports numerical tests in two and three dimensions that confirm the predicted convergence rates and demonstrate viscoelastic benchmarks plus mechanically driven calcium wavetrains.
watch_item: The method requires careful construction of compatible finite element spaces satisfying the inf-sup and weak-symmetry conditions, which may complicate implementation.
paper_title: Fully mixed finite element methods for the coupling of viscoelasticity and reaction-diffusion models
